newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Mogas silenced awaiting India.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Mogas silenced awaiting India.

text.p: The light distillate market was extremely quiet on Friday as traders awaited results from India's tender to buy 100,00 tonnes of gasoline for March delivery, traders said.
"Everybody is waiting for the award from IOC (Indian Oil Corp),' said a trader with a major oil company.
The award is due to be announced late Friday at around 1900 New Delhi time.
India's tender for four 25,000-tonne cargoes for delivery in the first half of March is expected to further tighten regional supplies.
Refinery shutdowns have momentarily swung Thailand from exporter to importer with a refiner heard seeking a 95-octane gasoline for first-half March arrival.
The shutdown of the 83,000-bpd cracker in Balongan, Indonesia has also left a major short of gasoline and prompted some purchases in the past two weeks.

Traders were also looking to Taiwan's reformate import tender closing next week. After its disappointing purchase of only one 250,000-barrel cargo of 95-octane unleaded reformate, it is expected to buy more than one cargo this time, they said.
But inspite of the lack of outright bids and offers, traders assessed gasoline around $2.75 per barrel higher tha naphtha.
Talk on naphtha was similarly dull with February barrels already committed and no deals heard yet on March.
Traders said they expected the lull to continue from buyers as term talks with Kuwait are due to start on Monday for one-year supplies starting in March.
Singapore March swaps gained 15 cents per barrel to $23.65/$23.85.
